Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (author, Wikidata Q254), died 1791; Ludwig Nohl (other, Wikidata Q97494), died 1885; Grace Wallace (translator, Wikidata Q5591227), died 1878. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Mozart, Wolfgang Amadeus, 1756-1791; Nohl, Ludwig, 1831-1885 [Compiler]; Wallace, Grace, Lady, 1804-1878 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The letters of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1769-1791), London, Longmans, Green, 1865, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cu31924017093703. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 87%, 88%, 100% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Ludwig Nohl, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
